english: supposing, supposing that, in the event that...
note: "Andai kata" is a slightly formal/literary way to say "supposing" or "what if"; everyday speech often uses "kalau" or "seandainya" instead.

sentences.text: Andai kata hujan, kita tidak ke pantai.
sentences.en: Supposing it rains, we won't go to the beach.

sentences.text: Andai kata dia datang, aku senang.
sentences.en: Supposing she comes, I would be happy.

sentences.text: Andai kata ada waktu, ayo ke pasar.
sentences.en: In the event that there is time, let's go to the market.

english: a small child, a little boy/girl
note: "Anak kecil" literally means "small child"; "anak" alone means "child", and "kecil" means "small/little" — commonly used in everyday speech for young children; related: "anak-anak" (children).

sentences.text: Ada anak kecil di taman itu.
sentences.en: There is a little child in that park.

sentences.text: Anak kecil itu makan es krim.
sentences.en: That little child is eating ice cream.

sentences.text: Ibu menjaga anak kecil di rumah.
sentences.en: Mother is looking after the small child at home.

english: what's on the agenda...?, what are (we/you, they) up to...?, what will (we/they) do...?
note: "Apa acara" is casual/informal, used to ask about plans or events; similar to "apa rencana" but more about scheduled activities or agenda items.

sentences.text: Apa acara kamu hari ini?
sentences.en: What are you up to today?

sentences.text: Apa acara keluarga kita minggu depan?
sentences.en: What's on the agenda for our family next week?

note: 'Barangkali' means 'maybe/perhaps' and is slightly more formal than 'mungkin'; often used in polite speech or soft suggestions.

sentences.text: Barangkali dia ada di rumah sekarang.
sentences.en: Maybe he is at home now.

sentences.text: Kita barangkali bisa makan bersama nanti.
sentences.en: We can maybe eat together later.

sentences.text: Barangkali besok cuaca lebih bagus.
sentences.en: Maybe tomorrow the weather will be better.

note: 'Berdansa' refers to Western or disco-style dancing (e.g., at a club or party); for traditional Indonesian dance, use 'menari' instead.

sentences.text: Mereka berdansa di pesta semalam.
sentences.en: They danced at the party last night.

sentences.text: Aku ingin berdansa di pantai.
sentences.en: I want to dance at the beach.

sentences.text: Dia berdansa dengan teman barunya.
sentences.en: She danced with her new friend.

note: 'Berjudi' is an informal/neutral verb meaning 'to gamble'; often considered negative in context, related words: 'judi' (gambling/noun), 'penjudi' (gambler).

sentences.text: Dia suka berjudi di kasino setiap malam.
sentences.en: He likes to gamble at the casino every night.

sentences.text: Ibu melarang anak-anak berjudi di rumah.
sentences.en: Mother forbids the children to gamble at home.

sentences.text: Berjudi bisa membuat orang kehilangan uang.
sentences.en: Gambling can make people lose money.

english: dancing, dance (popular western style), disco/ballroom dancing,
note: "Dansa" refers specifically to Western-style social dancing (ballroom, disco, clubbing), distinct from traditional Indonesian dance ("tari").

sentences.text: Kami suka dansa di pesta itu.
sentences.en: We like to dance at that party.

sentences.text: Dia belajar dansa setiap hari Sabtu.
sentences.en: She learns to dance every Saturday.

sentences.text: Mau dansa bersama saya?
sentences.en: Do you want to dance with me?

note: 'Hangat' means warm (temperature or atmosphere); also used figuratively for a warm welcome; don't confuse with 'panas' (hot).

sentences.text: Teh ini masih hangat dan enak.
sentences.en: This tea is still warm and delicious.

sentences.text: Cuaca hari ini terasa hangat sekali.
sentences.en: The weather today feels very warm.

sentences.text: Ibu membuat sup hangat untuk kami.
sentences.en: Mom made warm soup for us.

english: the food served at a meal
note: "Hidangan" is a slightly formal word for food/dishes served at a meal; everyday speech often uses "makanan" instead, but "hidangan" is common at events and restaurants.

sentences.text: Hidangan di pesta itu sangat lezat.
sentences.en: The food served at the party was very delicious.

sentences.text: Ibu menyiapkan hidangan untuk makan malam.
sentences.en: Mom is preparing the food for dinner.

sentences.text: Hidangan ini enak sekali.
sentences.en: This food served is very tasty.

english: the middle of the night, late at night
note: "Larut malam" means late at night (typically after midnight); more specific than "malam" (night) alone; often paired with "sampai" (until) to describe staying up late.

sentences.text: Dia tidur sangat larut malam tadi.
sentences.en: He slept very late last night.

sentences.text: Kami makan di warung larut malam.
sentences.en: We ate at a food stall late at night.

sentences.text: Jangan keluar rumah larut malam ya.
sentences.en: Don't go out of the house late at night, okay.

english: when (i.e. after something in the future has happened)
note: Used for future completed actions ('once/when X has happened'); often confused with 'kalau' alone (meaning 'if') or 'ketika' (meaning 'when' in the past/present).

sentences.text: Kalau sudah makan, kita pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: When we have eaten, we will go to the beach.

sentences.text: Kalau sudah sampai, tolong hubungi saya.
sentences.en: When you have arrived, please contact me.

sentences.text: Kalau sudah siap, kita mulai belajar.
sentences.en: When you are ready, we will start studying.

note: 'Kasino' is a loanword from English/Dutch; gambling is largely illegal in Indonesia, so casinos are rarely discussed in daily life.

sentences.text: Ada kasino besar di kota itu.
sentences.en: There is a big casino in that city.

sentences.text: Dia tidak mau pergi ke kasino.
sentences.en: He does not want to go to the casino.

note: 'Lotre' means lottery or raffle; common in everyday Indonesian, sometimes confused with 'undian' (draw/raffle), both are used interchangeably in casual speech.

sentences.text: Dia menang lotre hari ini.
sentences.en: He/She won the lottery today.

sentences.text: Saya beli tiket lotre di pasar.
sentences.en: I bought a lottery ticket at the market.

sentences.text: Lotre itu sangat populer di sini.
sentences.en: The lottery is very popular here.

note: 'Bulan depan' means 'next month'; 'bulan' also means 'moon', and 'depan' means 'front/next' — also used in 'minggu depan' (next week) and 'tahun depan' (next year).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke Bali bulan depan.
sentences.en: I am going to Bali next month.

sentences.text: Dia ulang tahun bulan depan.
sentences.en: Her birthday is next month.

sentences.text: Kami pindah rumah bulan depan.
sentences.en: We are moving house next month.

note: 'Minggu depan' means 'next week'; note that 'minggu' also means 'Sunday', so context matters — related: 'minggu lalu' (last week), 'minggu ini' (this week).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke Bali minggu depan.
sentences.en: I am going to Bali next week.

sentences.text: Dia mulai kerja minggu depan.
sentences.en: He/She starts work next week.

sentences.text: Kami ada ujian minggu depan.
sentences.en: We have an exam next week.

note: 'Tahun depan' means 'next year'; 'depan' literally means 'front/ahead', also used in 'minggu depan' (next week) and 'bulan depan' (next month).

sentences.text: Tahun depan saya mau ke Bali.
sentences.en: Next year I want to go to Bali.

sentences.text: Dia akan menikah tahun depan.
sentences.en: She will get married next year.

sentences.text: Tahun depan kami pindah rumah baru.
sentences.en: Next year we are moving to a new house.

note: 'Sarang' means nest (bird or insect); also used informally for a hideout or den; related: 'burung' (bird), 'lebah' (bee).

sentences.text: Burung itu membuat sarang di pohon.
sentences.en: That bird makes a nest in the tree.

sentences.text: Ada sarang lebah di dekat rumah.
sentences.en: There is a beehive near the house.

sentences.text: Anak-anak melihat sarang burung kecil.
sentences.en: The children see a small bird's nest.

english: what if, supposing, supposing that..., in the event that...
note: 'Seandainya' expresses hypothetical or wishful conditions (like 'if only / what if'); more formal/literary than 'kalau', often implies an unlikely or imagined scenario.

sentences.text: Seandainya aku punya uang, aku beli.
sentences.en: What if I had money, I would buy it.

sentences.text: Seandainya cuaca bagus, kita ke pantai.
sentences.en: If only the weather were nice, we'd go to the beach.

sentences.text: Seandainya dia datang, aku senang.
sentences.en: Supposing she came, I would be happy.

english: finished, completed (doing or making something), over,
note: "Selesai" means finished or over; it often follows "sudah" (already) to say something is done; don't confuse with "habis" which more often means 'run out of / used up'.

sentences.text: Saya sudah selesai makan siang.
sentences.en: I have already finished eating lunch.

sentences.text: Pekerjaan rumah saya sudah selesai.
sentences.en: My homework is already finished.

sentences.text: Film itu selesai jam delapan malam.
sentences.en: That movie is over at eight in the evening.

note: "Sop" is the common Indonesian spelling for soup, often seen on menus; related words include "soto" (a traditional spiced broth) and "kuah" (broth/gravy).

sentences.text: Saya makan sop ayam setiap hari.
sentences.en: I eat chicken soup every day.

sentences.text: Sop ini panas dan enak sekali.
sentences.en: This soup is hot and very delicious.

sentences.text: Ibu memasak sop untuk makan malam.
sentences.en: Mom cooks soup for dinner.

english: to take a holiday, to go on vacation
note: 'Berlibur' is an informal/neutral verb meaning to vacation or holiday; closely related to 'liburan' (the noun: a holiday/vacation), commonly used in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Kami berlibur ke Bali minggu depan.
sentences.en: We are going on vacation to Bali next week.

sentences.text: Dia berlibur bersama keluarganya.
sentences.en: She is on holiday with her family.

sentences.text: Saya ingin berlibur ke pantai.
sentences.en: I want to go on vacation to the beach.

note: 'Bulan' means both 'moon' and 'month'; context usually makes the meaning clear.

sentences.text: Bulan di langit sangat indah malam ini.
sentences.en: The moon in the sky is very beautiful tonight.

sentences.text: Saya lahir pada bulan Januari.
sentences.en: I was born in the month of January.

sentences.text: Bulan ini kami pergi ke Bali.
sentences.en: This month we are going to Bali.

note: "Bulan yang lalu" means "last month"; use it after the main verb or at the start of a sentence; don't confuse with "bulan lalu" (same meaning, slightly more informal).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke Bali bulan yang lalu.
sentences.en: I went to Bali last month.

sentences.text: Bulan yang lalu, dia beli sepeda baru.
sentences.en: Last month, he bought a new bicycle.

sentences.text: Kami makan di restoran itu bulan yang lalu.
sentences.en: We ate at that restaurant last month.

note: 'Hari Natal' means Christmas Day; 'hari' means 'day', used similarly in 'hari Minggu' (Sunday) and 'hari ulang tahun' (birthday); commonly celebrated in Indonesia despite Muslim majority.

sentences.text: Kami merayakan hari Natal bersama keluarga.
sentences.en: We celebrate Christmas Day with family.

sentences.text: Hari Natal adalah hari yang menyenangkan.
sentences.en: Christmas Day is a fun day.

sentences.text: Saya suka hari Natal.
sentences.en: I like Christmas Day.

note: 'Hari ulang tahun' (lit. 'day returns year') is the standard term for birthday; often shortened to 'HUT' in writing or 'ulang tahun' in casual speech; related: 'selamat ulang tahun' means 'happy birthday'.

sentences.text: Hari ini hari ulang tahun saya.
sentences.en: Today is my birthday.

sentences.text: Selamat hari ulang tahun, Budi!
sentences.en: Happy birthday, Budi!

sentences.text: Kita makan kue hari ulang tahun bersama.
sentences.en: We eat birthday cake together.

note: 'Kemerdekaan' means independence or freedom; commonly used for Indonesia's Independence Day (Hari Kemerdekaan); related: 'merdeka' (free/independent), 'bebas' (free/unrestricted).

sentences.text: Indonesia merayakan kemerdekaan setiap bulan Agustus.
sentences.en: Indonesia celebrates independence every August.

sentences.text: Hari kemerdekaan Indonesia sangat penting.
sentences.en: Indonesia's independence day is very important.

sentences.text: Kita harus menghargai kemerdekaan negara kita.
sentences.en: We must appreciate our country's independence.

note: 'Merdeka' means independent or free; used formally for national independence (Hari Merdeka) and informally to mean free/liberated; related: kemerdekaan (independence/noun).

sentences.text: Indonesia merdeka pada tanggal tujuh belas Agustus.
sentences.en: Indonesia became independent on the seventeenth of August.

sentences.text: Hari ini adalah hari merdeka kita.
sentences.en: Today is our independence day.

sentences.text: Kita harus bangga dengan negara merdeka ini.
sentences.en: We must be proud of this independent country.

note: 'Pindah' means to move or relocate (house, seat, city); common in everyday speech; related words: 'pindahan' (moving/relocation), 'memindahkan' (to move something).

sentences.text: Saya mau pindah ke rumah baru.
sentences.en: I want to move to a new house.

sentences.text: Dia pindah ke Bali tahun lalu.
sentences.en: She moved to Bali last year.

sentences.text: Boleh saya pindah kursi di sini?
sentences.en: May I move seats here?

note: 'Sering' means 'often/frequently'; place it before the verb; related: 'jarang' (rarely), 'selalu' (always), 'kadang-kadang' (sometimes).

sentences.text: Saya sering makan nasi goreng di sini.
sentences.en: I often eat fried rice here.

sentences.text: Dia sering pergi ke pasar pagi.
sentences.en: She often goes to the morning market.

sentences.text: Kami sering bermain di pantai.
sentences.en: We often play at the beach.

note: 'Tahun Baru' means 'New Year'; often paired with 'Selamat' (Happy) as 'Selamat Tahun Baru'; do not confuse 'tahun' (year) with 'tahu' (tofu/to know).

sentences.text: Selamat Tahun Baru untuk semua orang!
sentences.en: Happy New Year to everyone!

sentences.text: Kami merayakan Tahun Baru bersama keluarga.
sentences.en: We celebrate New Year together with family.

sentences.text: Tahun Baru ada banyak kembang api.
sentences.en: On New Year there are many fireworks.

note: 'Ujian' means exam or test; related to 'tes' (test) and 'ulangan' (quiz/repeated test); used in school contexts.

sentences.text: Besok saya ada ujian matematika.
sentences.en: Tomorrow I have a math exam.

sentences.text: Dia belajar keras untuk ujian.
sentences.en: She studies hard for the exam.

sentences.text: Ujian hari ini sangat sulit.
sentences.en: Today's exam is very difficult.

note: 'Yang akan datang' means 'next' or 'upcoming' for future events; more formal than 'berikutnya', often used with months, weeks, or events.

sentences.text: Bulan yang akan datang saya pergi ke Bali.
sentences.en: Next month I am going to Bali.

sentences.text: Festival yang akan datang sangat menarik.
sentences.en: The upcoming festival is very interesting.

sentences.text: Minggu yang akan datang kami belajar bersama.
sentences.en: Next week we will study together.

note: 'Januari' is the Indonesian word for January; all month names in Indonesian are borrowed from Dutch/English and are capitalized.

sentences.text: Hari ulang tahun saya di bulan Januari.
sentences.en: My birthday is in January.

sentences.text: Januari adalah bulan pertama dalam setahun.
sentences.en: January is the first month of the year.

sentences.text: Kami berlibur ke Bali pada Januari.
sentences.en: We vacation in Bali in January.

note: 'Februari' is the Indonesian word for February; months are not capitalized in all styles but commonly written with a capital letter; related words: Januari (January), Maret (March).

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan Februari.
sentences.en: My birthday is in February.

sentences.text: Kami liburan ke Bali bulan Februari.
sentences.en: We go on holiday to Bali in February.

sentences.text: Tanggal 14 Februari adalah Hari Valentine.
sentences.en: February 14th is Valentine's Day.

note: "Maret" is the Indonesian word for March; months in Indonesian are borrowed from Dutch/Latin and always capitalized.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan Maret.
sentences.en: My birthday is in March.

sentences.text: Kami pergi ke Bali bulan Maret.
sentences.en: We go to Bali in March.

sentences.text: Sekolah mulai lagi pada bulan Maret.
sentences.en: School starts again in March.

note: 'April' is the same in Indonesian as in English; months are not capitalized differently and are used the same way in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya pada bulan April.
sentences.en: My birthday is in April.

sentences.text: Hari raya itu jatuh pada bulan April.
sentences.en: That holiday falls in April.

sentences.text: Cuaca di April biasanya panas.
sentences.en: The weather in April is usually hot.

note: "Mei" is the fifth month of the year (May); it is a borrowed word and always capitalized as a proper noun.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya di bulan Mei.
sentences.en: My birthday is in May.

sentences.text: Liburan sekolah mulai bulan Mei.
sentences.en: The school holiday starts in May.

sentences.text: Hari ini tanggal sepuluh Mei.
sentences.en: Today is the tenth of May.

note: 'Juni' is the Indonesian word for June; months are borrowed from Dutch/English and are not capitalized in informal writing, but formally they are.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan Juni.
sentences.en: My birthday is in June.

sentences.text: Kami liburan ke Bali bulan Juni.
sentences.en: We go on holiday to Bali in June.

sentences.text: Juni adalah bulan keenam.
sentences.en: June is the sixth month.

note: 'Juli' is the Indonesian word for July; it is a proper noun and always capitalized, borrowed directly from Dutch/English.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan Juli.
sentences.en: My birthday is in July.

sentences.text: Kami pergi ke Bali bulan Juli.
sentences.en: We go to Bali in July.

sentences.text: Juli adalah bulan ketujuh.
sentences.en: July is the seventh month.

note: 'Agustus' is the eighth month; Indonesia's Independence Day (17 Agustus) makes it very commonly referenced.

sentences.text: Hari kemerdekaan Indonesia adalah tujuh belas Agustus.
sentences.en: Indonesia's Independence Day is the seventeenth of August.

sentences.text: Saya lahir pada bulan Agustus.
sentences.en: I was born in August.

sentences.text: Agustus adalah bulan kedelapan.
sentences.en: August is the eighth month.

note: 'September' is the same in Indonesian as in English; months are not capitalized differently and are used identically in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan September.
sentences.en: My birthday is in September.

sentences.text: Dia datang ke Bali bulan September.
sentences.en: He comes to Bali in September.

sentences.text: Sekolah mulai lagi bulan September.
sentences.en: School starts again in September.

note: 'Oktober' is a loanword from Dutch/English; months in Indonesian are capitalized and used the same way as in English.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya bulan Oktober.
sentences.en: My birthday is in October.

sentences.text: Mereka berlibur ke Bali bulan Oktober.
sentences.en: They go on holiday to Bali in October.

sentences.text: Oktober adalah bulan kesepuluh.
sentences.en: October is the tenth month.

note: 'November' is the same in Indonesian as in English; months are not capitalized differently but are always capitalized as proper nouns.

sentences.text: Hari ulang tahun saya bulan November.
sentences.en: My birthday is in November.

sentences.text: Hujan sering turun pada bulan November.
sentences.en: Rain often falls in the month of November.

note: "Desember" is the twelfth month; borrowed directly from Dutch/English, always capitalized in Indonesian.

sentences.text: Liburan saya ada di bulan Desember.
sentences.en: My holiday is in December.

sentences.text: Bali sangat ramai pada bulan Desember.
sentences.en: Bali is very crowded in December.

sentences.text: Ulang tahun saya di bulan Desember.
sentences.en: My birthday is in December.

english: tradition, old customs, traditional or customary law
note: 'Adat' refers to traditional customs or customary law in Indonesian culture; often heard in phrases like 'adat istiadat' (customs and traditions); very common in Balinese and Javanese contexts.

sentences.text: Ini adalah adat di desa kami.
sentences.en: This is the tradition in our village.

sentences.text: Kami mengikuti adat nenek moyang kami.
sentences.en: We follow the customs of our ancestors.

sentences.text: Pernikahan ini sesuai dengan adat setempat.
sentences.en: This wedding is in accordance with local tradition.

note: "Bensin" is the everyday Indonesian word for petrol/gasoline; used in casual speech across Indonesia, including Bali. Related word: "SPBU" (gas station). Do not confuse with "benzen" (benzene).

sentences.text: Saya perlu beli bensin di SPBU.
sentences.en: I need to buy petrol at the gas station.

sentences.text: Motor saya tidak ada bensin.
sentences.en: My motorbike has no petrol.

sentences.text: Harga bensin naik hari ini.
sentences.en: The petrol price went up today.

english: to stop, to come to a halt
note: 'Berhenti' means to stop or halt; often confused with 'berhenti' (quit a job) vs 'berhenti' (physically stop) — both uses are the same word; related: 'berhenti kerja' (quit work), 'berhenti sebentar' (stop for a moment).

sentences.text: Bus itu berhenti di depan pasar.
sentences.en: The bus stops in front of the market.

sentences.text: Tolong berhenti di sini, Pak.
sentences.en: Please stop here, sir.

sentences.text: Hujan sudah berhenti sekarang.
sentences.en: The rain has already stopped now.

note: 'Karcis' means ticket (bus, train, cinema, etc.); similar to 'tiket' but more traditional/local usage in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Saya beli karcis bus di sini.
sentences.en: I buy a bus ticket here.

sentences.text: Berapa harga karcis masuk kebun binatang?
sentences.en: How much is the entrance ticket to the zoo?

sentences.text: Karcis itu sudah habis terjual.
sentences.en: The tickets are already sold out.

note: 'Kuat' means strong or powerful; used for physical strength, flavors, or emotions; related words: 'kekuatan' (strength/power), 'kuatkan' (strengthen).

sentences.text: Ayah saya sangat kuat dan sehat.
sentences.en: My father is very strong and healthy.

sentences.text: Anak itu bisa angkat koper kuat.
sentences.en: That child can lift the heavy bag strongly.

sentences.text: Angin di Bali sangat kuat hari ini.
sentences.en: The wind in Bali is very strong today.

note: 'Menarik' means interesting/attractive; the root 'tarik' means to pull, so 'menarik' also means to pull — context determines meaning.

sentences.text: Pantai ini sangat menarik dan indah.
sentences.en: This beach is very interesting and beautiful.

sentences.text: Film itu menarik sekali untuk ditonton.
sentences.en: That movie is very interesting to watch.

sentences.text: Baju merah itu sangat menarik.
sentences.en: That red shirt is very attractive.

english: to stay (for one or more nights e.g. in a hotel or with a friend/relative), to sleep over
note: "Menginap" is the formal/standard form; the root "inap" appears in compounds like "penginapan" (lodging/guesthouse); commonly used for staying overnight at a hotel, friend's house, or relative's home.

sentences.text: Kami menginap di hotel dekat pantai.
sentences.en: We are staying at a hotel near the beach.

sentences.text: Malam ini saya menginap di rumah nenek.
sentences.en: Tonight I am sleeping over at grandma's house.

sentences.text: Mereka menginap dua malam di Bali.
sentences.en: They stayed two nights in Bali.

note: 'Perjalanan' is a neutral, everyday word for trip or journey; commonly used in travel contexts; related words include 'bepergian' (to travel) and 'wisata' (tourism/holiday trip).

sentences.text: Perjalanan ke Bali sangat menyenangkan.
sentences.en: The trip to Bali is very enjoyable.

sentences.text: Kami mulai perjalanan pagi ini.
sentences.en: We started the journey this morning.

sentences.text: Perjalanan dengan bus itu murah.
sentences.en: The trip by bus is cheap.

note: 'Pertama-tama' means 'first of all' and is used to introduce the first step or point; slightly more formal than 'dulu'; related to 'pertama' (first).

sentences.text: Pertama-tama, kita cuci tangan sebelum makan.
sentences.en: First of all, we wash our hands before eating.

sentences.text: Pertama-tama saya minum kopi pagi ini.
sentences.en: First of all, I drink coffee this morning.

note: 'Provinsi' means an administrative province in Indonesia; Indonesia has 38 provinces; often paired with 'di' (e.g. 'di provinsi ini').

sentences.text: Bali adalah sebuah provinsi di Indonesia.
sentences.en: Bali is a province in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Di provinsi ini ada banyak pantai.
sentences.en: In this province there are many beaches.

sentences.text: Saya tinggal di provinsi Jawa Barat.
sentences.en: I live in the province of West Java.

note: 'Rencana' means 'plan' or 'schedule'; common in everyday speech; related words: 'berencana' (to plan), 'merencanakan' (to plan something).

sentences.text: Apa rencana kamu hari ini?
sentences.en: What is your plan today?

sentences.text: Saya punya rencana pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: I have a plan to go to the beach.

sentences.text: Rencana kami batal karena hujan.
sentences.en: Our plan was cancelled because of rain.

english: to drop by, to make a short stop/visit, to call in (at a place)
note: "Singgah" is informal/neutral and means a brief, unplanned stop somewhere; similar to "mampir" (very casual), but slightly more literary; often used with "ke" to indicate the place visited.

sentences.text: Kami singgah ke warung dekat pantai.
sentences.en: We stopped by the warung near the beach.

sentences.text: Boleh saya singgah ke rumah kamu?
sentences.en: May I drop by your house?

sentences.text: Dia singgah sebentar di pasar.
sentences.en: She made a short stop at the market.

note: 'Tiba' means 'to arrive' and is slightly more formal than 'sampai'; often used in announcements; related phrase: 'tiba-tiba' means 'suddenly'.

sentences.text: Kereta api tiba di stasiun pagi ini.
sentences.en: The train arrives at the station this morning.

sentences.text: Kapan kamu tiba di Bali?
sentences.en: When did you arrive in Bali?

sentences.text: Tamu itu tiba di hotel kemarin.
sentences.en: The guest arrived at the hotel yesterday.

note: 'Agen' means agent or agency; used for travel agencies, ticketing agents, or sales representatives; similar to 'biro' for offices.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke agen perjalanan hari ini.
sentences.en: I went to the travel agency today.

sentences.text: Agen tiket itu tutup besok.
sentences.en: That ticket agency is closed tomorrow.

sentences.text: Dia bekerja sebagai agen properti.
sentences.en: She works as a property agent.

note: 'Alam' means nature or the natural world; commonly used in phrases like 'alam bebas' (open nature/wilderness) and 'alam semesta' (universe); not to be confused with 'alami' (natural/adjective form).

sentences.text: Alam di Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: Nature in Bali is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Saya suka berjalan di alam bebas.
sentences.en: I like walking in the open nature.

sentences.text: Anak-anak belajar tentang alam hari ini.
sentences.en: The children are learning about nature today.

note: 'Biro' means bureau or agency (e.g. travel agency, government office); often seen in 'biro perjalanan' (travel bureau); not to be confused with 'biro' meaning ballpoint pen in some contexts.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke biro perjalanan hari ini.
sentences.en: I am going to the travel bureau today.

sentences.text: Biro itu tutup pada hari Minggu.
sentences.en: The bureau is closed on Sunday.

sentences.text: Dia bekerja di biro pariwisata Bali.
sentences.en: She works at the Bali tourism bureau.

note: 'Danau' means lake; commonly seen in place names like Danau Batur (Bali) or Danau Toba (Sumatra); not to be confused with 'sungai' (river) or 'laut' (sea).

sentences.text: Danau ini sangat indah dan tenang.
sentences.en: This lake is very beautiful and calm.

sentences.text: Kami berenang di danau kemarin.
sentences.en: We swam in the lake yesterday.

sentences.text: Ada ikan besar di danau itu.
sentences.en: There are big fish in that lake.

note: 'Gunung' means mountain; commonly seen in place names like Gunung Agung; related word 'bukit' means hill.

sentences.text: Gunung Agung sangat tinggi dan indah.
sentences.en: Mount Agung is very tall and beautiful.

sentences.text: Saya ingin mendaki gunung besok pagi.
sentences.en: I want to climb the mountain tomorrow morning.

sentences.text: Pemandangan gunung itu sangat bagus.
sentences.en: The view of that mountain is very beautiful.

note: 'Hutan' means forest or jungle; commonly used in everyday speech; related words include 'pohon' (tree) and 'hewan' (animal).

sentences.text: Ada banyak pohon di hutan itu.
sentences.en: There are many trees in that forest.

sentences.text: Kami berjalan ke dalam hutan bersama.
sentences.en: We walked into the forest together.

sentences.text: Hutan di Bali sangat hijau dan indah.
sentences.en: The forest in Bali is very green and beautiful.

note: 'Losmen' refers to a small, budget guesthouse or inn, more basic than a 'hotel'; commonly found in tourist areas across Indonesia.

sentences.text: Kami menginap di losmen yang murah.
sentences.en: We are staying at a cheap small hotel.

sentences.text: Losmen ini dekat dengan pantai.
sentences.en: This small hotel is near the beach.

sentences.text: Saya mencari losmen untuk malam ini.
sentences.en: I am looking for a small hotel for tonight.

note: 'misalnya' means 'for example' and is used in everyday speech; similar to 'contohnya', both are interchangeable but 'misalnya' is slightly more conversational

sentences.text: Saya suka buah, misalnya mangga dan pisang.
sentences.en: I like fruit, for example mango and banana.

sentences.text: Ada banyak tempat wisata, misalnya Pantai Kuta.
sentences.en: There are many tourist spots, for example Kuta Beach.

note: 'Pantai' means beach or coast and is very common in everyday Indonesian; not to be confused with 'sungai' (river) or 'danau' (lake).

sentences.text: Saya suka pergi ke pantai setiap hari.
sentences.en: I like going to the beach every day.

sentences.text: Pantai di Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: The beach in Bali is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Kami bermain di pantai bersama keluarga.
sentences.en: We play at the beach together with family.

note: "Pemandangan alam" refers to natural scenery or landscape; more specific than "pemandangan" alone, which can mean any view; related: "alam" (nature), "indah" (beautiful).

sentences.text: Pemandangan alam di Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: The natural scenery in Bali is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Saya suka melihat pemandangan alam dari sini.
sentences.en: I like looking at the natural scenery from here.

sentences.text: Foto pemandangan alam ini bagus sekali.
sentences.en: This photo of natural scenery is really nice.

english: just one or two, just a few, a couple
note: 'Satu dua' is casual spoken Indonesian meaning 'just a few/couple'; often used to downplay quantity, similar to saying 'only one or two' in English.

sentences.text: Saya hanya punya satu dua teman di sini.
sentences.en: I only have a couple of friends here.

sentences.text: Dia makan satu dua potong roti saja.
sentences.en: She ate just one or two pieces of bread.

sentences.text: Ada satu dua turis di pantai itu.
sentences.en: There are just a few tourists at that beach.

note: 'Pariwisata' is a noun meaning 'tourism', but often used as an adjective modifier in phrases like 'daerah pariwisata' (tourist area); related words: 'wisata' (trip/tour), 'wisatawan' (tourist/person).

sentences.text: Bali adalah daerah pariwisata yang terkenal.
sentences.en: Bali is a famous tourist area.

sentences.text: Kota ini punya banyak objek pariwisata.
sentences.en: This city has many tourist attractions.

sentences.text: Industri pariwisata sangat penting di Indonesia.
sentences.en: The tourist industry is very important in Indonesia.

note: 'Wisatawan' means tourist or visitor; commonly used in formal and everyday speech; related words: 'turis' (informal for tourist), 'wisata' (tourism/trip)

sentences.text: Banyak wisatawan datang ke Bali setiap hari.
sentences.en: Many tourists come to Bali every day.

sentences.text: Wisatawan itu membeli oleh-oleh di pasar.
sentences.en: That tourist buys souvenirs at the market.

sentences.text: Pemandu membantu wisatawan menemukan jalan.
sentences.en: The guide helps the tourist find the way.

note: 'Aneh' is a common informal adjective meaning strange or weird; often confused with 'asing' (foreign/unfamiliar); related word: 'keanehan' (strangeness).

sentences.text: Rasanya aneh, aku tidak suka.
sentences.en: It tastes strange, I don't like it.

sentences.text: Ada suara aneh di luar rumah.
sentences.en: There is a strange sound outside the house.

sentences.text: Kenapa dia bertingkah aneh hari ini?
sentences.en: Why is he acting weird today?

note: "Benar" means 'true' or 'correct'; often confused with "betul" (same meaning); commonly used in "benar atau salah" (true or false).

sentences.text: Jawaban kamu benar sekali.
sentences.en: Your answer is absolutely correct.

sentences.text: Apakah berita itu benar?
sentences.en: Is that news true?

sentences.text: Ya, itu benar.
sentences.en: Yes, that is true.

note: 'Daripada' means 'than' in comparisons; beginners often confuse it with 'dari' (from/of), but 'daripada' is specifically used for comparing two things.

sentences.text: Apel ini lebih murah daripada jeruk itu.
sentences.en: This apple is cheaper than that orange.

sentences.text: Bali lebih panas daripada Jakarta.
sentences.en: Bali is hotter than Jakarta.

sentences.text: Saya lebih suka teh daripada kopi.
sentences.en: I prefer tea more than coffee.

english: crude, oafish, impolite, rough to the touch
note: "Kasar" covers both physical roughness (texture) and rude/rough behavior; opposite is "halus" (smooth, refined, polite).

sentences.text: Permukaan batu itu sangat kasar.
sentences.en: The surface of that stone is very rough.

sentences.text: Jangan bicara kasar kepada orang tua.
sentences.en: Don't speak rudely to elderly people.

sentences.text: Anak itu kasar kepada temannya.
sentences.en: That child is rude to his friend.

note: 'Ketimbang' is informal/colloquial for 'daripada' (than/rather than); common in spoken Indonesian, especially in Java and Bali.

sentences.text: Saya lebih suka nasi ketimbang roti.
sentences.en: I prefer rice rather than bread.

sentences.text: Berjalan kaki lebih sehat ketimbang naik motor.
sentences.en: Walking is healthier than riding a motorbike.

sentences.text: Buah ini lebih murah ketimbang di pasar.
sentences.en: This fruit is cheaper than at the market.

note: 'Kok' is a casual, slightly surprised 'how come/why'; used in spoken Indonesian, not formal writing; similar to 'kenapa' but more expressive of surprise.

sentences.text: Kok kamu tidak makan nasi?
sentences.en: How come you're not eating rice?

sentences.text: Kok toko ini tutup hari ini?
sentences.en: How come this shop is closed today?

sentences.text: Kamu kok pulang cepat sekali.
sentences.en: How come you came home so early?

note: 'Lebih' means 'more' or '-er' in comparisons; often paired with 'dari' (than), e.g. 'lebih besar dari' (bigger than); do not confuse with 'lagi' (more/again in other contexts).

sentences.text: Kopi ini lebih manis dari teh.
sentences.en: This coffee is sweeter than tea.

sentences.text: Bali lebih panas dari Jakarta hari ini.
sentences.en: Bali is hotter than Jakarta today.

sentences.text: Saya mau lebih banyak nasi, terima kasih.
sentences.en: I want more rice, thank you.

note: "Lebih banyak" means "more" in quantity; use "lebih" alone before adjectives, but pair it with "banyak" when referring to a greater amount or number of things.

sentences.text: Saya mau lebih banyak nasi, terima kasih.
sentences.en: I want more rice, thank you.

sentences.text: Di pasar ada lebih banyak buah segar.
sentences.en: At the market there is more fresh fruit.

sentences.text: Dia minum lebih banyak air setiap hari.
sentences.en: She drinks more water every day.

english: (informal) A slangy exclamation which, when it appears at the beginning of a phrase or sentence, expresses mild surprise and incredulity
note: "Lho" is a very informal spoken particle; place it at the start of a sentence to show mild surprise or disbelief, similar to English "Hey!" or "Wait, really?"

sentences.text: Lho, kamu sudah di sini?
sentences.en: Hey, you're already here?

sentences.text: Lho, ini bukan tas saya!
sentences.en: Wait, this isn't my bag!

sentences.text: Lho, warung itu sudah tutup?
sentences.en: Hey, that warung is already closed?

note: "Mana" means "which" or "where" depending on context; often confused with "apa" (what); used in questions like "yang mana" (which one).

sentences.text: Baju mana yang kamu suka?
sentences.en: Which shirt do you like?

sentences.text: Mana restoran yang enak di sini?
sentences.en: Which restaurant is good here?

sentences.text: Kamu mau pergi ke mana?
sentences.en: Where do you want to go?

english: (informal) I don't believe you/it!, come off it!, you're kidding me!

note: "Membosankan" is an adjective meaning 'boring'; it is formed from "bosan" (bored/tired of) with the me-kan affix, making it transitive/descriptive — don't confuse "bosan" (feeling bored) with "membosankan" (something that IS boring).

sentences.text: Film ini sangat membosankan bagi saya.
sentences.en: This film is very boring for me.

sentences.text: Pelajaran itu membosankan dan lama.
sentences.en: That lesson is boring and long.

sentences.text: Cuaca hujan membuat hari ini membosankan.
sentences.en: Rainy weather makes today boring.

note: 'Modern' is borrowed directly from English; used widely in Indonesian to describe new, up-to-date things or styles.

sentences.text: Rumah ini sangat modern dan bagus.
sentences.en: This house is very modern and nice.

sentences.text: Pasar modern itu menjual banyak barang.
sentences.en: That modern market sells many goods.

sentences.text: Dia suka gaya hidup modern.
sentences.en: She likes a modern lifestyle.

note: 'Pokoknya' is informal/colloquial, used to summarize or stress the main point; similar to 'intinya' (the point is); very common in spoken Indonesian.

sentences.text: Pokoknya kita harus pergi sekarang.
sentences.en: The main thing is we have to go now.

sentences.text: Pokoknya makanan ini enak sekali.
sentences.en: The main thing is this food is very delicious.

sentences.text: Pokoknya jangan lupa bawa uang.
sentences.en: The main thing is don't forget to bring money.

note: "Pendapat" means opinion or view; often used in discussions; related: "menurut saya" (in my opinion), "opini"

sentences.text: Apa pendapat kamu tentang makanan ini?
sentences.en: What is your opinion about this food?

sentences.text: Pendapat saya, pantai Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: In my opinion, Bali's beach is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Dia ingin tahu pendapat saya.
sentences.en: He wants to know my opinion.

note: 'Ramah' means friendly/welcoming; commonly used to describe people or service; related phrase 'ramah tamah' means warm hospitality.

sentences.text: Ibu itu sangat ramah kepada semua orang.
sentences.en: That woman is very friendly to everyone.

sentences.text: Pelayan di restoran ini ramah sekali.
sentences.en: The waiter at this restaurant is very friendly.

sentences.text: Orang Bali terkenal ramah dan baik hati.
sentences.en: Balinese people are known to be friendly and kind.

note: "Sekamar" combines "se-" (one/same) + "kamar" (room); used to mean sharing a room with someone, common in homestay or dormitory contexts.

sentences.text: Aku sekamar dengan teman di hostel.
sentences.en: I share a room with a friend at the hostel.

sentences.text: Dia sekamar dengan kakaknya setiap liburan.
sentences.en: She shares a room with her older sibling every holiday.

sentences.text: Kami sekamar di hotel Bali.
sentences.en: We share one room at a hotel in Bali.

english: to be of the same opinion
note: "Sependapat" is a formal-leaning word meaning to agree or share the same view; related to "pendapat" (opinion); more polite than "setuju" in discussions.

sentences.text: Saya sependapat dengan kamu soal itu.
sentences.en: I am of the same opinion as you about that.

sentences.text: Kami sependapat tentang rencana liburan ini.
sentences.en: We are of the same opinion about this holiday plan.

note: 'Serumah' combines 'se-' (same/one) + 'rumah' (house); used in everyday speech to mean living together under one roof, often about family or roommates.

sentences.text: Saya serumah dengan kakak saya.
sentences.en: I live in one house with my older sibling.

sentences.text: Mereka serumah di Bali sejak lama.
sentences.en: They have lived in one house in Bali for a long time.

sentences.text: Kami serumah dan selalu makan bersama.
sentences.en: We live in one house and always eat together.

english: to be of the same age
note: "Seumur" means "of the same age" and is commonly paired with "hidup" (life) to form "seumur hidup" (lifelong/forever); avoid confusing it with "umur" (age) alone.

sentences.text: Kami berdua seumur, sama-sama dua puluh tahun.
sentences.en: We are both the same age, both twenty years old.

sentences.text: Teman saya seumur dengan kakak saya.
sentences.en: My friend is the same age as my older sibling.

sentences.text: Mereka seumur, lahir di tahun yang sama.
sentences.en: They are the same age, born in the same year.

note: 'Sip' is very informal/colloquial Indonesian slang meaning 'fine', 'great', or 'agreed'; often used to confirm plans or show approval, similar to a thumbs-up.

sentences.text: Oke, sip! Kita makan bersama besok.
sentences.en: Okay, great! We eat together tomorrow.

sentences.text: Makanan di sini sip sekali.
sentences.en: The food here is really great.

sentences.text: Jam tiga? Sip, sampai jumpa nanti.
sentences.en: Three o'clock? Fine, see you later.

note: 'Teman sekelas' means classmate; 'teman' alone means friend, 'sekelas' means same class; very common in school contexts.

sentences.text: Dia adalah teman sekelas saya di sekolah.
sentences.en: She is my classmate at school.

sentences.text: Teman sekelas saya sangat baik dan ramah.
sentences.en: My classmate is very kind and friendly.

sentences.text: Saya makan siang dengan teman sekelas saya.
sentences.en: I have lunch with my classmate.

note: Informal intensifier meaning 'really/truly'; similar to 'sungguh-sungguh' but more conversational; often used to emphasize feelings or facts.

sentences.text: Makanan ini betul-betul enak sekali.
sentences.en: This food is really, truly delicious.

sentences.text: Saya betul-betul lelah hari ini.
sentences.en: I am genuinely tired today.

sentences.text: Pantai Bali betul-betul indah.
sentences.en: The beach in Bali is truly beautiful.

note: 'Hati-hati' means 'be careful' or 'careful/cautious'; used as a warning or adjective; related: 'hati' means 'heart/liver', so literally 'heart-heart'; very common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Hati-hati, jalannya licin sekali!
sentences.en: Be careful, the road is very slippery!

sentences.text: Tolong hati-hati di pasar itu.
sentences.en: Please be careful at that market.

sentences.text: Ibu bilang hati-hati naik motor.
sentences.en: Mom said be careful riding the motorbike.

note: 'Jelas' means 'clear' or 'clear/understood'; commonly used in both formal and casual speech; related words: 'kejelasan' (clarity), 'memperjelas' (to clarify); sometimes confused with 'tentu' (certainly).

sentences.text: Suara guru itu sangat jelas.
sentences.en: The teacher's voice is very clear.

sentences.text: Apakah penjelasan saya sudah jelas?
sentences.en: Is my explanation already clear?

sentences.text: Foto ini tidak jelas.
sentences.en: This photo is not clear.

note: Used to indicate greater distance or extent; 'lebih' = more, 'jauh' = far, 'lagi' = even/more; similar to 'lebih jauh' but 'lagi' adds extra emphasis.

sentences.text: Pantai itu lebih jauh lagi dari sini.
sentences.en: That beach is even further away from here.

sentences.text: Pasar ada lebih jauh lagi dari hotel.
sentences.en: The market is even further away from the hotel.

sentences.text: Rumahnya lebih jauh lagi dari sekolah.
sentences.en: His house is even further away from the school.

note: Used to express 'even more' or a greater degree of something; common in everyday speech; related to 'lebih' (more) and 'banyak' (a lot/many).

sentences.text: Saya ingin makan lebih banyak lagi nasi.
sentences.en: I want to eat even more rice.

sentences.text: Di pasar ada lebih banyak lagi buah.
sentences.en: At the market there is even more fruit.

sentences.text: Dia minum air lebih banyak lagi hari ini.
sentences.en: She drinks even more water today.

note: 'lebih mahal lagi' means 'even more expensive'; 'lebih' = more, 'mahal' = expensive, 'lagi' adds emphasis; commonly used when comparing prices at markets or shops

sentences.text: Harga di sana lebih mahal lagi.
sentences.en: The price there is even more expensive.

sentences.text: Tas ini lebih mahal lagi dari kemarin.
sentences.en: This bag is even more expensive than yesterday.

sentences.text: Di mall, semua lebih mahal lagi.
sentences.en: At the mall, everything is even more expensive.

note: "Mengerti" means to understand; similar to "paham" (more formal); used in casual and formal speech alike.

sentences.text: Apakah kamu mengerti pelajaran hari ini?
sentences.en: Do you understand today's lesson?

sentences.text: Saya tidak mengerti bahasa Bali.
sentences.en: I don't understand Balinese language.

sentences.text: Dia sudah mengerti cara memasak nasi.
sentences.en: She already understands how to cook rice.

note: 'Museum' is the same in Indonesian and English; it is a neutral/formal word used for cultural and historical sites, common in tourism contexts.

sentences.text: Kami pergi ke museum hari ini.
sentences.en: We are going to the museum today.

sentences.text: Museum ini sangat besar dan menarik.
sentences.en: This museum is very big and interesting.

sentences.text: Tiket masuk museum itu murah sekali.
sentences.en: The entrance ticket to that museum is very cheap.

note: 'Sangat' means 'very/extremely' and is interchangeable with 'sekali' (placed after the adjective); it comes before the adjective, e.g. 'sangat bagus' not 'bagus sangat'.

sentences.text: Pantai ini sangat indah dan bersih.
sentences.en: This beach is very beautiful and clean.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng di sini sangat enak.
sentences.en: The fried rice here is very delicious.

sentences.text: Hari ini sangat panas di Bali.
sentences.en: Today is very hot in Bali.

note: 'Sanggup' means 'able/capable of doing something'; slightly more formal than 'bisa', often implies willingness and ability together.

sentences.text: Saya sanggup membawa tas berat ini.
sentences.en: I am able to carry this heavy bag.

sentences.text: Apakah kamu sanggup datang besok?
sentences.en: Are you able to come tomorrow?

sentences.text: Dia sanggup memasak nasi goreng sendiri.
sentences.en: She is able to cook fried rice by herself.

note: 'Setuju' means 'agree' or 'agreed'; used in both formal and casual speech; related: 'tidak setuju' (disagree), 'saya setuju' (I agree).

sentences.text: Saya setuju dengan ide kamu.
sentences.en: I agree with your idea.

sentences.text: Apakah kamu setuju dengan rencana ini?
sentences.en: Do you agree with this plan?

sentences.text: Kami semua setuju untuk pergi bersama.
sentences.en: We all agree to go together.

note: 'Terlalu' means 'too' or 'too much' and always comes before an adjective or adverb; don't confuse it with 'sangat' (very).

sentences.text: Makanan ini terlalu pedas untuk saya.
sentences.en: This food is too spicy for me.

sentences.text: Harga ini terlalu mahal bagi saya.
sentences.en: This price is too expensive for me.

sentences.text: Saya terlalu lelah untuk jalan-jalan.
sentences.en: I am too tired to go for a walk.

english: to be honest, to be quite frank, frankly speaking
note: "Terus terang" is a common informal phrase meaning "frankly" or "to be honest"; often placed at the start of a sentence, similar to "honestly" in English.

sentences.text: Terus terang, saya tidak suka durian.
sentences.en: To be honest, I don't like durian.

sentences.text: Terus terang, saya lelah sekali hari ini.
sentences.en: Frankly speaking, I am very tired today.

sentences.text: Dia berkata terus terang kepada saya.
sentences.en: He spoke frankly to me.

note: 'Cuaca' means 'weather' and is used in everyday conversation; related words include 'hujan' (rain), 'panas' (hot), and 'dingin' (cold).

sentences.text: Cuaca hari ini sangat panas sekali.
sentences.en: The weather today is very hot.

sentences.text: Cuaca di Bali selalu cerah dan indah.
sentences.en: The weather in Bali is always sunny and beautiful.

sentences.text: Bagaimana cuaca di sana sekarang?
sentences.en: How is the weather there now?

english: in addition to that, moreover, furthermore
note: "Di samping itu" is a formal/written connective meaning 'moreover'; in casual speech Indonesians often say "selain itu" instead.

sentences.text: Dia pintar. Di samping itu, dia rajin.
sentences.en: She is smart. Moreover, she is hardworking.

sentences.text: Makanan ini enak. Di samping itu, murah.
sentences.en: This food is delicious. Furthermore, it is cheap.

note: 'Halus' can mean 'refined/polite' for people or 'smooth/fine' for textures; here we focus on the 'refined, well-spoken' sense, often used to describe someone with good manners.

sentences.text: Ibu guru itu sangat halus cara bicaranya.
sentences.en: That teacher is very refined in the way she speaks.

sentences.text: Dia orang yang halus dan sopan.
sentences.en: She is a refined and polite person.

sentences.text: Anak itu berbicara dengan halus kepada semua orang.
sentences.en: That child speaks in a refined way to everyone.

note: 'Hampir' means 'almost/nearly'; used before verbs or adjectives; don't confuse with 'dekat' (physically close).

sentences.text: Saya hampir lupa membawa dompet saya.
sentences.en: I almost forgot to bring my wallet.

sentences.text: Bus itu hampir penuh hari ini.
sentences.en: The bus is almost full today.

sentences.text: Dia hampir sampai di pantai.
sentences.en: He is almost at the beach.

note: 'Lengkap' means complete or full set; often used for documents or equipment; related: 'tidak lengkap' (incomplete), 'melengkapi' (to complete)

sentences.text: Dokumen saya sudah lengkap.
sentences.en: My documents are already complete.

sentences.text: Warung ini menjual bumbu yang lengkap.
sentences.en: This small shop sells a complete range of spices.

sentences.text: Tolong bawa perlengkapan yang lengkap besok.
sentences.en: Please bring complete equipment tomorrow.

note: 'Parlemen' refers to the legislative parliament; formal/news register, related to 'DPR' (the Indonesian parliament building/body).

sentences.text: Parlemen membuat undang-undang untuk rakyat Indonesia.
sentences.en: The parliament makes laws for the Indonesian people.

sentences.text: Saya menonton berita tentang parlemen tadi malam.
sentences.en: I watched the news about the parliament last night.

sentences.text: Gedung parlemen ada di Jakarta.
sentences.en: The parliament building is in Jakarta.

note: 'Sopan' means polite/courteous; use it to describe people or behavior; related words: 'kesopanan' (politeness), 'tidak sopan' (rude).

sentences.text: Dia selalu sopan kepada orang tua.
sentences.en: She is always polite to older people.

sentences.text: Berbicara sopan itu sangat penting.
sentences.en: Speaking politely is very important.

sentences.text: Anak itu sopan dan baik hati.
sentences.en: That child is polite and kind.

note: "Tidak kalah" literally means "not losing/inferior", used to say something is just as good as another; common in comparisons, often followed by 'dari' (than) or 'dengan' (with).

sentences.text: Nasi goreng ini tidak kalah enak.
sentences.en: This fried rice is just as delicious.

sentences.text: Pantai ini tidak kalah indah dari Kuta.
sentences.en: This beach is just as beautiful as Kuta.

sentences.text: Warung kecil ini tidak kalah ramai.
sentences.en: This small food stall is just as busy.

note: "Aman" means safe or secure; commonly used in everyday situations; related words include "keamanan" (security/safety) and "mengamankan" (to secure/safeguard).

sentences.text: Jalan ini aman untuk anak-anak.
sentences.en: This road is safe for children.

sentences.text: Tempat ini aman dan nyaman.
sentences.en: This place is safe and comfortable.

sentences.text: Apakah air ini aman untuk diminum?
sentences.en: Is this water safe to drink?

note: 'Baik hati' means kind or good-hearted; more expressive than just 'baik' (good), often used to describe generous or caring people.

sentences.text: Ibu saya sangat baik hati kepada semua orang.
sentences.en: My mother is very kind to everyone.

sentences.text: Pak Made adalah guru yang baik hati.
sentences.en: Mr. Made is a kind teacher.

sentences.text: Tetangga saya baik hati dan suka membantu.
sentences.en: My neighbor is kind and likes to help.

note: 'Berbahaya' means dangerous; used as an adjective or predicate; related: 'bahaya' (danger/noun), 'membahayakan' (to endanger).

sentences.text: Jalan itu berbahaya di malam hari.
sentences.en: That road is dangerous at night.

sentences.text: Api sangat berbahaya untuk anak kecil.
sentences.en: Fire is very dangerous for small children.

sentences.text: Berenang di sini berbahaya karena ombak besar.
sentences.en: Swimming here is dangerous because of big waves.

note: 'Binatang' means animal in general; 'hewan' is a slightly more formal synonym; avoid confusing with 'binatan' (not a word).

sentences.text: Ada banyak binatang di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: There are many animals at the zoo.

sentences.text: Kucing adalah binatang peliharaan yang lucu.
sentences.en: A cat is a cute pet animal.

sentences.text: Anak itu suka binatang.
sentences.en: That child likes animals.

note: 'Bosan' means bored or tired of something; often confused with 'lelah' (physically tired) — 'bosan' is mental/emotional fatigue or tedium.

sentences.text: Saya bosan menunggu di sini.
sentences.en: I am bored waiting here.

sentences.text: Dia bosan makan nasi setiap hari.
sentences.en: He is sick of eating rice every day.

sentences.text: Anak itu bosan di rumah.
sentences.en: That child is bored at home.

note: 'Dokter' is the standard formal and everyday word for a medical doctor; not to be confused with 'dukun' (traditional healer); related: 'dokter gigi' (dentist).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke dokter hari ini.
sentences.en: I am going to the doctor today.

sentences.text: Dokter itu sangat baik dan ramah.
sentences.en: That doctor is very kind and friendly.

sentences.text: Ibu saya adalah seorang dokter.
sentences.en: My mother is a doctor.

note: 'Hiburan' means entertainment or amusement; commonly used for movies, music, or shows; related: 'menghibur' (to entertain), 'terhibur' (to be entertained).

sentences.text: Nonton film adalah hiburan yang menyenangkan.
sentences.en: Watching a movie is fun entertainment.

sentences.text: Musik adalah hiburan favorit saya.
sentences.en: Music is my favorite entertainment.

sentences.text: Anak-anak suka hiburan di pantai.
sentences.en: Children like entertainment at the beach.

note: "Jangan lupa" means "don't forget"; "jangan" is used before verbs to form negative commands, similar to "don't".

sentences.text: Jangan lupa minum air setiap hari.
sentences.en: Don't forget to drink water every day.

sentences.text: Jangan lupa bawa uang ke pasar.
sentences.en: Don't forget to bring money to the market.

sentences.text: Jangan lupa tutup pintu rumah.
sentences.en: Don't forget to close the house door.

note: 'Kejahatan' means 'crime' or 'wrongdoing'; more formal than 'kriminal' (criminal); related words: 'jahat' (evil/bad), 'penjahat' (criminal/villain).

sentences.text: Kejahatan itu tidak baik untuk masyarakat.
sentences.en: Crime is not good for society.

sentences.text: Polisi selalu melawan kejahatan di kota.
sentences.en: The police always fight crime in the city.

sentences.text: Jangan lakukan kejahatan di sini.
sentences.en: Don't commit crime here.

note: 'Ladang' means an open field or dry farmland (not wet rice field); contrast with 'sawah' (wet rice paddy field); common in rural/farming contexts.

sentences.text: Ayah bekerja di ladang setiap hari.
sentences.en: Father works in the field every day.

sentences.text: Ladang itu sangat luas dan hijau.
sentences.en: The field is very wide and green.

sentences.text: Kami menanam jagung di ladang besar.
sentences.en: We plant corn in the big field.

note: 'Lingkungan' means environment or neighborhood/surroundings; commonly used for both natural environment and local community area; related words: alam (nature), sekitar (around).

sentences.text: Kita harus menjaga lingkungan kita bersama.
sentences.en: We must take care of our environment together.

sentences.text: Lingkungan di Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: The environment in Bali is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain di lingkungan rumah.
sentences.en: The children play around the neighborhood.

note: 'Menangkap' is the formal/active form; 'tangkap' is the base root used in casual speech and commands (e.g., 'Tangkap dia!'); commonly used for catching animals, criminals, or objects.

sentences.text: Anak itu menangkap kupu-kupu di taman.
sentences.en: That child catches a butterfly in the park.

sentences.text: Nelayan menangkap ikan di laut setiap hari.
sentences.en: The fisherman catches fish in the sea every day.

sentences.text: Dia menangkap bola yang dilempar temannya.
sentences.en: He catches the ball thrown by his friend.

note: "Rusak" means broken/damaged (adjective); "merusak" is the active verb form meaning to damage/destroy something; don't confuse with "hancur" (completely destroyed).

sentences.text: Anak itu merusak mainan barunya.
sentences.en: That child broke his new toy.

sentences.text: Jangan merusak tanaman di taman ini.
sentences.en: Don't damage the plants in this garden.

sentences.text: Hujan deras bisa merusak atap rumah.
sentences.en: Heavy rain can damage the roof of a house.

note: 'Miskin' means poor/impoverished; more formal than 'tidak punya uang'; opposite is 'kaya' (rich); commonly used in social or news contexts.

sentences.text: Keluarga itu sangat miskin dan butuh bantuan.
sentences.en: That family is very poor and needs help.

sentences.text: Dia tidak miskin, dia punya banyak uang.
sentences.en: He is not poor, he has a lot of money.

sentences.text: Banyak orang miskin tinggal di sini.
sentences.en: Many poor people live here.

note: 'Mudah' means easy/simple; opposite is 'sulit' or 'susah'; often paired with 'sangat' (very) as in 'sangat mudah'

sentences.text: Soal ini sangat mudah untuk saya.
sentences.en: This question is very easy for me.

sentences.text: Bahasa Indonesia mudah dipelajari setiap hari.
sentences.en: Indonesian is easy to learn every day.

sentences.text: Resep masakan ini mudah dan cepat.
sentences.en: This cooking recipe is easy and quick.

note: 'Pekerjaan' is a formal/neutral noun for work or job; 'kerja' is the base verb/informal form; often confused with 'tugas' (task/assignment).

sentences.text: Apa pekerjaan kamu sekarang?
sentences.en: What is your job now?

sentences.text: Saya mencari pekerjaan baru di Bali.
sentences.en: I am looking for a new job in Bali.

sentences.text: Pekerjaan dia adalah guru.
sentences.en: Her job is a teacher.

note: 'Penjahat' means criminal/villain; root word 'jahat' means evil/bad; common in news and stories; do not confuse with 'nakal' (naughty).

sentences.text: Polisi menangkap penjahat itu kemarin.
sentences.en: The police caught that criminal yesterday.

sentences.text: Penjahat itu lari sangat cepat.
sentences.en: That criminal ran very fast.

sentences.text: Film ini tentang seorang penjahat berbahaya.
sentences.en: This film is about a dangerous criminal.

note: 'Petani' means farmer; related words include 'bertani' (to farm) and 'pertanian' (agriculture); neutral everyday register.

sentences.text: Bapak saya adalah seorang petani padi.
sentences.en: My father is a rice farmer.

sentences.text: Petani itu bekerja di sawah setiap hari.
sentences.en: The farmer works in the rice field every day.

sentences.text: Petani menjual sayuran di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: The farmer sells vegetables at the morning market.

english: broken, out of order, not working, damaged
note: "Rusak" covers broken, damaged, or out of order things; commonly confused with "patah" (snapped/broken in two) or "pecah" (shattered); often used for appliances, vehicles, and roads.

sentences.text: Sepeda motor saya rusak di jalan.
sentences.en: My motorbike broke down on the road.

sentences.text: AC di kamar ini rusak.
sentences.en: The air conditioner in this room is broken.

sentences.text: Handphone saya rusak kemarin.
sentences.en: My phone broke yesterday.

note: 'Sakit' means sick or ill and also means pain/hurt (e.g. 'sakit kepala' = headache); very common in everyday speech across all registers.

sentences.text: Saya sakit hari ini dan istirahat.
sentences.en: I am sick today and resting.

sentences.text: Ibu saya sakit perut kemarin.
sentences.en: My mother had a stomachache yesterday.

sentences.text: Dia tidak sekolah karena sakit.
sentences.en: He/She did not go to school because of being sick.

note: 'Sehat' means healthy or in good health; commonly used in the greeting 'semoga sehat selalu' (hope you stay healthy) and related to 'kesehatan' (health/healthcare).

sentences.text: Saya makan sayur supaya tetap sehat.
sentences.en: I eat vegetables to stay healthy.

sentences.text: Ibu saya selalu sehat dan bahagia.
sentences.en: My mother is always healthy and happy.

sentences.text: Minum air putih membuat badan sehat.
sentences.en: Drinking water keeps the body healthy.

english: to be scared, to be afraid
note: 'Takut' is an adjective/verb meaning 'scared' or 'afraid'; commonly paired with 'saya' (I) or followed by a noun, e.g. 'takut anjing' (afraid of dogs); related: 'ketakutan' (fear/frightened).

sentences.text: Saya takut dengan anjing besar itu.
sentences.en: I am scared of that big dog.

sentences.text: Adik saya takut naik motor.
sentences.en: My younger sibling is afraid to ride a motorbike.

sentences.text: Dia takut sendirian di rumah malam ini.
sentences.en: She is scared to be alone at home tonight.

note: 'Tenang' means calm or tranquil; used for people, places, or situations; related word 'ketenangan' means peace/calmness; common in everyday speech to tell someone to relax.

sentences.text: Pantai ini sangat tenang pada pagi hari.
sentences.en: This beach is very calm in the morning.

sentences.text: Tolong tenang, bayi sedang tidur.
sentences.en: Please be calm, the baby is sleeping.

sentences.text: Saya suka suasana yang tenang di sini.
sentences.en: I like the calm atmosphere here.

note: 'Terburu-buru' means rushing or being in a hurry; related to 'buru-buru' (same meaning, slightly less formal); avoid confusing with 'tergesa-gesa' which is nearly identical but more literary.

sentences.text: Dia terburu-buru pergi ke pasar.
sentences.en: She is in a hurry to go to the market.

sentences.text: Jangan terburu-buru, masih ada waktu.
sentences.en: Don't be in a hurry, there is still time.

sentences.text: Saya terburu-buru karena bis hampir berangkat.
sentences.en: I am in a hurry because the bus is about to leave.

note: 'Udara' means 'air' (the atmosphere); not to be confused with 'angin' (wind); commonly used in phrases about weather and breathing.

sentences.text: Udara di Bali sangat segar pagi ini.
sentences.en: The air in Bali is very fresh this morning.

sentences.text: Saya suka udara dingin di pegunungan.
sentences.en: I like the cold air in the mountains.

sentences.text: Udara di sini bersih dan sejuk.
sentences.en: The air here is clean and cool.

note: "Jangan" means "don't" and is used before a verb to give a negative command; common in everyday speech for warnings and advice.

sentences.text: Jangan lupa minum air setiap hari.
sentences.en: Don't forget to drink water every day.

sentences.text: Jangan makan di sini, ya.
sentences.en: Don't eat here, okay.

sentences.text: Jangan pergi sekarang, tunggu sebentar.
sentences.en: Don't go now, wait a moment.

note: 'Kera' means ape or monkey (often macaque); do not confuse with 'kerja' (work) or 'keras' (hard/loud); related: 'monyet' (monkey, more common in casual speech).

sentences.text: Kera itu makan pisang di pohon.
sentences.en: The ape is eating a banana in the tree.

sentences.text: Anak-anak melihat kera di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: The children are looking at the ape at the zoo.

sentences.text: Kera itu lucu dan lincah sekali.
sentences.en: That ape is very cute and agile.

english: better, it would be better if/to..., should
note: 'Lebih baik' means 'better' or 'it is better to/if'; used in casual and formal speech to give advice or compare options; related: 'lebih' (more), 'baik' (good)

sentences.text: Lebih baik kamu minum air putih sekarang.
sentences.en: You should drink plain water now.

sentences.text: Lebih baik kita pergi pagi-pagi.
sentences.en: It is better if we go early in the morning.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng ini lebih baik dari kemarin.
sentences.en: This fried rice is better than yesterday.

note: "Orang utan" literally means "forest person" in Malay/Indonesian; it is both the animal name and the origin of the English word "orangutan"; not to be confused with "orang" meaning "person/people".

sentences.text: Saya melihat orang utan di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: I saw an orang-outang at the zoo.

sentences.text: Orang utan itu makan pisang.
sentences.en: The orang-outang is eating a banana.

sentences.text: Orang utan hidup di hutan Kalimantan.
sentences.en: Orang-outangs live in the forests of Kalimantan.

english: preferably, it would be good if..., it would be better to..., should
note: 'Sebaiknya' expresses a soft recommendation or advice ('it would be better to...'); milder than 'harus' (must) and more common in everyday speech than 'seharusnya'.

sentences.text: Kamu sebaiknya minum air putih banyak.
sentences.en: You should drink a lot of water.

sentences.text: Sebaiknya kita berangkat pagi-pagi.
sentences.en: It would be better if we leave early in the morning.

sentences.text: Kamu sebaiknya istirahat sekarang.
sentences.en: You should rest now.

english: the real thing, genuine, not imitation
note: 'Asli' means genuine or authentic; often used in markets to distinguish real goods from fakes; related: 'palsu' (fake/imitation).

sentences.text: Ini batik asli dari Solo.
sentences.en: This batik is genuine, from Solo.

sentences.text: Apakah kopi ini asli Bali?
sentences.en: Is this coffee really from Bali?

sentences.text: Saya mau beli yang asli saja.
sentences.en: I want to buy only the real thing.

note: 'Bandar udara' is the formal term for airport; the informal shorthand 'bandara' is more common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke bandar udara besok.
sentences.en: I am going to the airport tomorrow.

sentences.text: Bandar udara ini sangat besar.
sentences.en: This airport is very big.

sentences.text: Taksi ke bandar udara mahal sekali.
sentences.en: A taxi to the airport is very expensive.

note: "Daerah" means region, area, or district; used for neighborhoods, zones, or rural areas; related words: "wilayah" (territory), "kawasan" (zone/area).

sentences.text: Saya tinggal di daerah Ubud.
sentences.en: I live in the Ubud region.

sentences.text: Daerah ini sangat indah dan tenang.
sentences.en: This area is very beautiful and peaceful.

sentences.text: Banyak wisatawan datang ke daerah kami.
sentences.en: Many tourists come to our region.

note: 'Gunung api' literally means 'fire mountain'; also commonly shortened to 'gunung berapi' — both are correct and widely used.

sentences.text: Di Bali ada gunung api yang terkenal.
sentences.en: In Bali there is a famous volcano.

sentences.text: Gunung api itu sangat tinggi dan indah.
sentences.en: That volcano is very tall and beautiful.

sentences.text: Kami melihat gunung api dari hotel.
sentences.en: We saw the volcano from the hotel.

note: 'Karyawan' is neutral/formal for employee; 'pegawai' often refers to government workers; 'pekerja' is a broader term for worker.

sentences.text: Dia adalah karyawan di hotel itu.
sentences.en: He/She is an employee at that hotel.

sentences.text: Karyawan itu bekerja setiap hari.
sentences.en: That employee works every day.

sentences.text: Toko ini punya lima karyawan baru.
sentences.en: This shop has five new employees.

note: 'Kayu' means wood or timber; commonly used in everyday speech; related words include 'pohon' (tree) and 'meja kayu' (wooden table).

sentences.text: Meja ini dibuat dari kayu.
sentences.en: This table is made of wood.

sentences.text: Ayah membeli kayu di pasar.
sentences.en: Father buys wood at the market.

sentences.text: Rumah itu terbuat dari kayu.
sentences.en: That house is made of wood.

note: 'Kerajinan tangan' literally means 'hand craft'; commonly used in markets, schools, and tourism contexts; related words: 'seni' (art), 'buatan tangan' (handmade).

sentences.text: Ibu menjual kerajinan tangan di pasar.
sentences.en: Mother sells handicrafts at the market.

sentences.text: Saya suka membuat kerajinan tangan dari bambu.
sentences.en: I like making handicrafts from bamboo.

sentences.text: Toko itu menjual kerajinan tangan Bali.
sentences.en: That shop sells Balinese handicrafts.

note: 'Kesenian' means art or fine art; related to 'seni' (art), often used for traditional/cultural art forms; not to be confused with 'ilmu pengetahuan' (science/knowledge).

sentences.text: Saya suka belajar kesenian di sekolah.
sentences.en: I like learning art at school.

sentences.text: Bali terkenal dengan kesenian yang indah.
sentences.en: Bali is famous for its beautiful art.

sentences.text: Ibu mengajar kesenian setiap hari Senin.
sentences.en: Mom teaches art every Monday.

note: 'Langsung' means 'direct/directly/right away'; often confused with 'segera' (soon/immediately); used in casual and formal speech alike.

sentences.text: Dia langsung pergi ke pasar pagi ini.
sentences.en: She went directly to the market this morning.

sentences.text: Saya mau langsung pulang ke rumah.
sentences.en: I want to go straight home.

sentences.text: Makan langsung setelah masak ya!
sentences.en: Eat right away after cooking, okay!

english: community, society, public, people of a certain place
note: "Masyarakat" is a neutral, slightly formal word for a community or society; commonly used in news and school contexts; related words include "warga" (residents/citizens) and "rakyat" (the people/populace).

sentences.text: Masyarakat Bali suka merayakan hari raya.
sentences.en: The Balinese community likes to celebrate holidays.

sentences.text: Masyarakat di sini sangat ramah.
sentences.en: The people here are very friendly.

sentences.text: Dokter itu membantu masyarakat setiap hari.
sentences.en: That doctor helps the community every day.

note: "Mengadakan" is a formal/semi-formal verb meaning to hold or organize an event; "adakan" is the imperative/colloquial short form; often used with meetings (rapat), parties (pesta), or ceremonies (upacara).

sentences.text: Kami mengadakan pesta ulang tahun besok.
sentences.en: We are holding a birthday party tomorrow.

sentences.text: Sekolah mengadakan rapat dengan orang tua.
sentences.en: The school is holding a meeting with the parents.

sentences.text: Desa kami mengadakan upacara adat hari ini.
sentences.en: Our village is holding a traditional ceremony today.

english: the cost of a service, the charge of a service, the fare
note: 'Ongkos' refers to a fee for a service or transport fare; similar to 'biaya' (general cost) but more specific to services like rides or labor.

sentences.text: Berapa ongkos naik ojek ke pasar?
sentences.en: How much is the fare to ride an ojek to the market?

sentences.text: Ongkos taksi hari ini mahal sekali.
sentences.en: The taxi fare today is very expensive.

sentences.text: Saya tidak punya uang untuk ongkos.
sentences.en: I don't have money for the fare.

note: 'Orang asing' literally means 'foreign person'; used in everyday speech, neutral register; related: 'wisatawan' (tourist), 'bule' (informal for Western foreigner).

sentences.text: Orang asing itu suka makan nasi goreng.
sentences.en: That foreigner likes to eat fried rice.

sentences.text: Banyak orang asing berlibur di Bali.
sentences.en: Many foreigners vacation in Bali.

sentences.text: Orang asing itu berbicara bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: That foreigner speaks Indonesian.

note: 'Pura' specifically means a Balinese Hindu temple; not to be confused with 'masjid' (mosque) or 'gereja' (church); related: 'odalan' (temple ceremony).

sentences.text: Kami mengunjungi pura yang indah di Bali.
sentences.en: We visited a beautiful temple in Bali.

sentences.text: Pura ini sangat besar dan tua.
sentences.en: This temple is very big and old.

sentences.text: Setiap hari ada orang berdoa di pura.
sentences.en: Every day there are people praying at the temple.

note: "Rumah adat" refers to traditional or customary houses specific to each Indonesian ethnic group; often confused with "rumah biasa" (ordinary house); related: "adat" (custom/tradition), "budaya" (culture).

sentences.text: Ini adalah rumah adat Bali yang indah.
sentences.en: This is a beautiful Balinese traditional house.

sentences.text: Kami mengunjungi rumah adat di desa.
sentences.en: We visited a traditional house in the village.

sentences.text: Rumah adat itu sangat tua.
sentences.en: That traditional house is very old.

english: everything, all the components or items
note: 'Segala-galanya' means 'everything' with an emphasis on totality; more emphatic than 'semua', often used emotionally or to stress completeness.

sentences.text: Keluarga adalah segala-galanya bagi saya.
sentences.en: Family is everything to me.

sentences.text: Dia sudah menyiapkan segala-galanya untuk pesta.
sentences.en: She has prepared everything for the party.

sentences.text: Uang bukan segala-galanya dalam hidup.
sentences.en: Money is not everything in life.

note: 'Tarif' means a fixed cost or rate (e.g. taxi fare, hotel rate); more formal than 'harga' (price) and often used for services, transport, or utilities.

sentences.text: Berapa tarif taksi ke bandara?
sentences.en: How much is the taxi fare to the airport?

sentences.text: Tarif hotel ini sangat murah.
sentences.en: The rate of this hotel is very cheap.

sentences.text: Saya tanya tarif kamar kepada resepsionis.
sentences.en: I asked the receptionist about the room rate.

note: "Tempat" means 'where' as a relative pronoun (e.g., 'the place where'); it differs from 'di mana' used in questions, and is often interchangeable with 'di mana' in relative clauses.

sentences.text: Ini restoran tempat saya makan kemarin.
sentences.en: This is the restaurant where I ate yesterday.

sentences.text: Itu pasar tempat ibu membeli sayuran.
sentences.en: That is the market where my mother buys vegetables.

sentences.text: Dia tinggal di desa tempat saya lahir.
sentences.en: He lives in the village where I was born.

note: "Terbuat dari" means "made from/of" and is used to describe a material or ingredient; do not confuse with "dibuat oleh" which means "made by" (a person).

sentences.text: Tas ini terbuat dari kulit sapi.
sentences.en: This bag is made from cowhide.

sentences.text: Tempe terbuat dari kedelai.
sentences.en: Tempeh is made from soybeans.

sentences.text: Patung itu terbuat dari kayu jati.
sentences.en: That statue is made from teak wood.

note: 'Terletak' means 'located/situated' and is used to describe where something is; it is more formal than 'ada' but very common in everyday descriptions of places.

sentences.text: Hotel itu terletak di dekat pantai.
sentences.en: That hotel is located near the beach.

sentences.text: Warung ini terletak di tengah desa.
sentences.en: This small restaurant is located in the middle of the village.

sentences.text: Pura itu terletak di atas bukit.
sentences.en: That temple is located on top of the hill.

note: 'Upacara' means ceremony or ritual; commonly used for school flag ceremonies ('upacara bendera') and religious/traditional events; not to be confused with 'pesta' (party).

sentences.text: Hari Senin ada upacara bendera di sekolah.
sentences.en: On Monday there is a flag ceremony at school.

sentences.text: Upacara adat itu sangat indah.
sentences.en: That traditional ceremony is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Kami ikut upacara bersama keluarga.
sentences.en: We join the ceremony together with family.

note: 'Atas' meaning 'for' is used in phrases like 'terima kasih atas...' (thank you for...) and 'maaf atas...' (sorry for...); don't confuse with 'atas' meaning 'above/top'.

sentences.text: Terima kasih atas bantuanmu hari ini.
sentences.en: Thank you for your help today.

sentences.text: Maaf atas kesalahan saya kemarin.
sentences.en: Sorry for my mistake yesterday.

sentences.text: Terima kasih atas makanan yang enak.
sentences.en: Thank you for the delicious food.

note: 'Badak' means rhinoceros; commonly heard in zoo or wildlife contexts; related word: 'badak bercula satu' (one-horned rhinoceros).

sentences.text: Saya melihat badak di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: I saw a rhinoceros at the zoo.

sentences.text: Badak itu sangat besar dan kuat.
sentences.en: That rhinoceros is very big and strong.

sentences.text: Anak-anak suka foto dengan badak.
sentences.en: Children like to take photos with the rhinoceros.

note: 'Bahwa' means 'that' as a conjunction linking clauses; more formal than spoken 'kalau'; common in news, school, and written Indonesian.

sentences.text: Dia tahu bahwa toko itu sudah tutup.
sentences.en: He knows that the shop is already closed.

sentences.text: Ibu bilang bahwa makan sudah siap.
sentences.en: Mom said that the food is ready.

sentences.text: Saya pikir bahwa Bali sangat indah.
sentences.en: I think that Bali is very beautiful.

note: 'Bajak laut' literally means 'sea plower'; used in stories and movies, not everyday speech; related: 'perompak' (pirate/raider), 'kapal bajak laut' (pirate ship).

sentences.text: Anak itu suka cerita bajak laut.
sentences.en: That child likes pirate stories.

sentences.text: Film bajak laut itu sangat seru.
sentences.en: That pirate movie is very exciting.

sentences.text: Dia berpakaian seperti bajak laut.
sentences.en: He is dressed like a pirate.

note: 'Bantuan' is a neutral everyday noun meaning help or assistance; related verb is 'bantu' (to help); common phrase: 'minta bantuan' (to ask for help).

sentences.text: Saya minta bantuan dari teman saya.
sentences.en: I ask for help from my friend.

sentences.text: Terima kasih atas bantuan Anda.
sentences.en: Thank you for your help.

sentences.text: Dia butuh bantuan di pasar.
