sentences.en: She needs help at the market.

note: "Barat" means west/western as a direction or region; commonly seen in place names like "Jakarta Barat" (West Jakarta); not to be confused with "barat" in some regional dialects.

sentences.text: Matahari terbenam di sebelah barat.
sentences.en: The sun sets in the west.

sentences.text: Hotel itu ada di Jakarta Barat.
sentences.en: That hotel is in West Jakarta.

sentences.text: Angin dari barat terasa dingin.
sentences.en: The wind from the west feels cold.

english: at a loss what to do, worried and undecided, undecided who/what to believe, confused
note: 'Bingung' is a very common informal word for feeling confused or unsure; often interchangeable with 'tidak tahu harus apa'; related: 'bingung sekali' (very confused), 'membingungkan' (confusing).

sentences.text: Saya bingung mau makan apa hari ini.
sentences.en: I don't know what to eat today.

sentences.text: Dia bingung karena tidak mengerti pelajaran itu.
sentences.en: She is confused because she doesn't understand that lesson.

sentences.text: Kami bingung mencari jalan ke pantai.
sentences.en: We are lost trying to find the way to the beach.

note: 'Bunyi' means sound or noise; often confused with 'suara' (voice/sound from a person), but 'bunyi' is used for non-human sounds like alarms, animals, or machines.

sentences.text: Bunyi alarm itu sangat keras pagi ini.
sentences.en: The alarm noise is very loud this morning.

sentences.text: Apa bunyi itu? Ada kucing di luar.
sentences.en: What is that noise? There is a cat outside.

sentences.text: Saya dengar bunyi motor di jalan.
sentences.en: I hear the sound of a motorbike on the road.

english: to the left and right of, on both sides of, all around
note: 'di kanan-kiri' means 'on both sides of' something; commonly used in directions and descriptions; related: 'kanan' (right), 'kiri' (left), 'di sekitar' (around)

sentences.text: Di kanan-kiri jalan ada banyak pohon.
sentences.en: On both sides of the road there are many trees.

sentences.text: Di kanan-kiri pasar ada warung makan.
sentences.en: On both sides of the market there are food stalls.

sentences.text: Di kanan-kiri rumah ada kebun bunga.
sentences.en: On both sides of the house there is a flower garden.

note: "Gajah" means elephant; commonly seen in Bali at elephant parks; related words: "kebun binatang" (zoo), "hewan" (animal).

sentences.text: Gajah itu sangat besar dan kuat.
sentences.en: That elephant is very big and strong.

sentences.text: Saya melihat gajah di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: I saw an elephant at the zoo.

sentences.text: Anak gajah itu lucu sekali.
sentences.en: That baby elephant is very cute.

note: 'Harimau' is the standard word for tiger; 'macan' is a common informal/regional synonym used in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Harimau itu besar dan sangat kuat.
sentences.en: That tiger is big and very strong.

sentences.text: Anak-anak melihat harimau di kebun binatang.
sentences.en: The children see a tiger at the zoo.

sentences.text: Harimau suka makan daging.
sentences.en: Tigers like to eat meat.

note: 'Hilang' is a common everyday word for something lost or disappeared; often confused with 'tersesat' (lost/wandering, for people); related: 'kehilangan' (to lose/experience loss).

sentences.text: Kunci saya hilang di pantai tadi.
sentences.en: My key disappeared at the beach earlier.

sentences.text: Kucing itu hilang sejak kemarin.
sentences.en: That cat has been gone since yesterday.

sentences.text: Dompet saya hilang di pasar.
sentences.en: My wallet got lost at the market.

note: 'Ibu kota' literally means 'mother city'; it is the standard neutral term for capital city, not to be confused with 'kota' (city) alone.

sentences.text: Jakarta adalah ibu kota Indonesia.
sentences.en: Jakarta is the capital city of Indonesia.

sentences.text: Saya ingin pergi ke ibu kota.
sentences.en: I want to go to the capital city.

sentences.text: Ibu kota itu sangat ramai.
sentences.en: The capital city is very busy.

note: 'Letusan' means eruption (of a volcano); related to 'meletus' (to erupt); commonly heard in Indonesia due to active volcanoes like Merapi.

sentences.text: Letusan gunung itu sangat besar kemarin.
sentences.en: The eruption of the mountain was very big yesterday.

sentences.text: Kami melihat letusan gunung dari jauh.
sentences.en: We saw the eruption of the volcano from far away.

sentences.text: Letusan itu membuat semua orang takut.
sentences.en: The eruption made everyone scared.

note: "Di luar negeri" means abroad/overseas; contrast with "di dalam negeri" (domestically); used in everyday speech across all registers.

sentences.text: Kakak saya bekerja di luar negeri.
sentences.en: My older sibling works overseas.

sentences.text: Dia belajar di luar negeri sekarang.
sentences.en: He/She is studying abroad now.

sentences.text: Mereka tinggal di luar negeri lama.
sentences.en: They lived abroad for a long time.

note: 'Mati' means 'to die' or 'dead' and is also used for machines/lights turning off; less formal than 'meninggal' for people.

sentences.text: Lampu di kamar saya mati tadi malam.
sentences.en: The light in my room went out last night.

sentences.text: Ikan kecil itu mati kemarin.
sentences.en: That small fish died yesterday.

sentences.text: Baterai ponsel saya hampir mati.
sentences.en: My phone battery is almost dead.

note: "Meletus" means to erupt or explode; commonly used for volcanoes (gunung berapi meletus) or balloons popping; the root word is "letus".

sentences.text: Gunung berapi itu meletus kemarin pagi.
sentences.en: That volcano erupted yesterday morning.

sentences.text: Balon itu meletus karena terlalu besar.
sentences.en: That balloon popped because it was too big.

note: 'Membunuh' is the formal verb form; 'bunuh' is the root; avoid confusing with 'memburu' (to hunt); often seen in news or crime stories.

sentences.text: Dia membunuh seekor nyamuk di kamar.
sentences.en: He killed a mosquito in the room.

sentences.text: Kucing itu membunuh tikus kecil.
sentences.en: That cat killed a small mouse.

sentences.text: Jangan bunuh semut di lantai.
sentences.en: Don't kill the ants on the floor.

note: "Mendengar" is the formal/written form; "dengar" is the casual spoken form; often confused with "mendengarkan" (to listen attentively).

sentences.text: Saya mendengar musik dari kamar sebelah.
sentences.en: I hear music from the next room.

sentences.text: Apa kamu dengar suara itu?
sentences.en: Did you hear that sound?

sentences.text: Dia tidak mendengar bel pintu tadi.
sentences.en: He did not hear the doorbell just now.

english: let's hope that, I hope that
note: Informal expression of hope, similar to 'hopefully'; commonly used in everyday speech; related to 'semoga' which is slightly more formal.

sentences.text: Mudah-mudahan cuaca hari ini bagus.
sentences.en: Hopefully the weather today is nice.

sentences.text: Mudah-mudahan makanan ini enak sekali.
sentences.en: I hope this food is very delicious.

sentences.text: Mudah-mudahan kita tidak terlambat.
sentences.en: Let's hope we are not late.

english: because of this/that, for this reason, that is why...
note: 'Oleh karena itu' is a formal connective meaning 'therefore'; in casual speech Indonesians often say 'makanya' or 'jadi' instead.

sentences.text: Hujan deras, oleh karena itu kami di rumah.
sentences.en: It rained heavily, so we stayed home.

sentences.text: Dia sakit, oleh karena itu tidak ke sekolah.
sentences.en: She is sick, that is why she didn't go to school.

note: 'Penumpang' means passenger or rider; the root 'tumpang' means to ride along or hitch a ride; commonly used for buses, boats, and planes.

sentences.text: Penumpang bus itu duduk dengan tenang.
sentences.en: The bus passenger sits calmly.

sentences.text: Berapa penumpang di dalam kapal itu?
sentences.en: How many passengers are on that boat?

sentences.text: Penumpang harus menunggu di sini.
sentences.en: Passengers must wait here.

note: 'Selat' means a narrow stretch of water between two landmasses; not to be confused with 'salat' (prayer) or 'salad' (salad).

sentences.text: Selat Lombok sangat dalam dan luas.
sentences.en: The Lombok Strait is very deep and wide.

sentences.text: Kapal feri menyeberangi selat itu.
sentences.en: The ferry crosses that strait.

sentences.text: Kami melihat selat dari atas bukit.
sentences.en: We saw the strait from the top of the hill.

note: 'Selatan' means 'south' or 'southern'; used in directions and place names like 'Jakarta Selatan'; do not confuse with 'barat' (west) or 'timur' (east).

sentences.text: Pantai itu ada di selatan Bali.
sentences.en: That beach is in the south of Bali.

sentences.text: Rumah saya di Jakarta Selatan.
sentences.en: My house is in South Jakarta.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah selatan.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the south direction.

english: to come/go down, to descend, to get out (of a vehicle), to disembark
note: 'Turun' is the opposite of 'naik' (to go up/board); used for descending stairs, getting off buses, or rain falling.

sentences.text: Saya turun dari bus di sini.
sentences.en: I get off the bus here.

sentences.text: Anak itu turun dari tangga pelan-pelan.
sentences.en: The child comes down the stairs slowly.

sentences.text: Hujan turun setiap sore di Bali.
sentences.en: Rain falls every afternoon in Bali.

note: "Berapa kali?" asks about frequency or number of times; often confused with "berapa kali" used mid-sentence (e.g., 'sudah berapa kali?'); related: 'berapa?' (how much/many?), 'sekali' (once), 'dua kali' (twice).

sentences.text: Kamu sudah makan berapa kali hari ini?
sentences.en: How many times have you eaten today?

sentences.text: Bis ke Ubud datang berapa kali sehari?
sentences.en: How many times a day does the bus to Ubud come?

sentences.text: Kamu sudah ke Bali berapa kali?
sentences.en: How many times have you been to Bali?

note: "Bisnis" is a common loanword from English used in everyday speech; more formal than "usaha" but both mean business/enterprise.

sentences.text: Dia punya bisnis kecil di pasar.
sentences.en: She has a small business at the market.

sentences.text: Bisnis warung makan itu sangat ramai.
sentences.en: That food stall business is very busy.

sentences.text: Saya ingin mulai bisnis sendiri.
sentences.en: I want to start my own business.

note: 'Internasional' is a formal loanword from English; used in everyday speech for airports, schools, and events; related: 'dunia' (world).

sentences.text: Bandara internasional ada di Denpasar.
sentences.en: The international airport is in Denpasar.

sentences.text: Sekolah internasional itu sangat bagus.
sentences.en: That international school is very good.

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke festival internasional.
sentences.en: She went to the international festival.

note: 'Jalur' means lane or path; commonly used for traffic lanes, bus lanes, or bike lanes; related words: 'jalan' (road), 'lajur' (also lane, more formal).

sentences.text: Mobil itu masuk ke jalur yang salah.
sentences.en: That car entered the wrong lane.

sentences.text: Jalur bus ini sangat sibuk setiap hari.
sentences.en: This bus lane is very busy every day.

sentences.text: Tolong ikuti jalur yang benar di sini.
sentences.en: Please follow the correct lane here.

note: Literally 'economy class'; used for budget airline seats; contrast with 'kelas bisnis' (business class) or 'kelas satu' (first class).

sentences.text: Saya beli tiket kelas ekonomi ke Bali.
sentences.en: I bought an economy class ticket to Bali.

sentences.text: Kursi kelas ekonomi lebih murah.
sentences.en: Economy class seats are cheaper.

sentences.text: Kami naik pesawat di kelas ekonomi.
sentences.en: We flew in economy class.

note: 'Khususnya' means 'especially/in particular'; slightly formal but common in speech; related to 'khusus' (special/specific).

sentences.text: Saya suka buah, khususnya mangga.
sentences.en: I like fruit, especially mango.

sentences.text: Bali indah, khususnya pantainya.
sentences.en: Bali is beautiful, especially its beaches.

sentences.text: Dia suka makanan, khususnya nasi goreng.
sentences.en: He likes food, especially fried rice.

note: 'Komposisi' is a formal/neutral word used in art, music, and cooking contexts; beginners often encounter it when describing ingredients or arrangements.

sentences.text: Komposisi foto ini sangat bagus.
sentences.en: The composition of this photo is very good.

sentences.text: Saya suka komposisi warna bajunya.
sentences.en: I like the color composition of the shirt.

sentences.text: Komposisi makanan ini sehat sekali.
sentences.en: The composition of this food is very healthy.

note: "Paket" is used for packages, bundles, or meal/service combos (e.g. a meal deal); borrowed from Dutch, very common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya menerima paket dari toko online.
sentences.en: I received a package from an online store.

sentences.text: Paket ini untuk siapa?
sentences.en: Who is this package for?

sentences.text: Kami pesan paket nasi ayam.
sentences.en: We ordered a chicken rice combo.

note: 'Populer' is a loanword from English, used in both formal and informal speech; similar to 'terkenal' (famous/well-known).

sentences.text: Nasi goreng adalah makanan yang sangat populer.
sentences.en: Fried rice is a very popular food.

sentences.text: Pantai Kuta sangat populer di Bali.
sentences.en: Kuta Beach is very popular in Bali.

sentences.text: Lagu ini populer di kalangan anak muda.
sentences.en: This song is popular among young people.

note: 'Sebagai' means 'as' in the sense of a role or capacity; not to be confused with 'seperti' (like/similar to).

sentences.text: Dia bekerja sebagai guru di sekolah.
sentences.en: He works as a teacher at school.

sentences.text: Saya datang sebagai tamu di sini.
sentences.en: I came as a guest here.

sentences.text: Bali terkenal sebagai pulau yang indah.
sentences.en: Bali is famous as a beautiful island.

note: 'Tempat duduk' literally means 'sitting place'; used for seats in buses, cinemas, and restaurants; 'kursi' is a related word meaning 'chair'.

sentences.text: Tempat duduk saya ada di baris dua.
sentences.en: My seat is in row two.

sentences.text: Apakah tempat duduk ini kosong?
sentences.en: Is this seat empty?

sentences.text: Tolong simpan tempat duduk saya.
sentences.en: Please save my seat.

note: 'Terbang' means 'to fly'; used for birds, planes, and insects; related words: 'penerbangan' (flight), 'pesawat terbang' (airplane).

sentences.text: Burung itu terbang di langit biru.
sentences.en: That bird flies in the blue sky.

sentences.text: Pesawat kami terbang ke Bali besok.
sentences.en: Our plane flies to Bali tomorrow.

sentences.text: Kupu-kupu kecil terbang di taman ini.
sentences.en: A small butterfly flies in this garden.

note: 'Tertarik' means 'interested in' or 'attracted to'; use 'tertarik dengan/pada' before a noun; don't confuse with 'menarik' (interesting/attractive) which describes the thing itself.

sentences.text: Saya tertarik dengan budaya Bali.
sentences.en: I am interested in Balinese culture.

sentences.text: Dia tertarik belajar bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: She is interested in learning Indonesian.

sentences.text: Kami tertarik dengan makanan lokal di sini.
sentences.en: We are interested in the local food here.
